deep.reconstruction:
Context: this folio is the opening of §2 of an early draft of what became 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872), whose §2 has the same title, 'Vergleichung der rationalen Zahlen mit den Punkten einer geraden Linie'. §1, on the previous page, listed order properties of the rationals Q: trichotomy, transitivity, betweenness, intervals (a,c), 'Stücke' (pieces), and the decomposition of Q by a number a into classes A1 = {x < a} and A2 = {x > a}.

This page has no computations. It gives a parallel axiomatics of order for the points of a straight line L.

(1) Orientation. Fix the two opposite directions and call them 'right' and 'left'. For distinct points α ≠ β, exactly one of the following holds:
- α is right of β (equivalently, β is left of α), or
- α is left of β.
Which one holds depends on whether the segment from β to α points right or left. In modern terms: there is a strict total order < on L, with 'α right of β' meaning β < α.

(2) Transitivity. If α is right of β and β is right of γ, then α is right of γ (γ < β < α implies γ < α). In that case β is said to lie between α and γ.

(3) Segments. All points between α and γ form a 'Strecke'; 'Stück' was inserted as an alternative word. This is the open order-interval (γ, α), the analogue of the interval/Stück of §1.

(4) Cut by a point. Each point α splits L into two pieces:
- P1 = {points left of α},
- P2 = {points right of α},
and every point of P2 lies to the right of every point of P1. This is the exact analogue of §1.V (the decomposition of Q by a rational a into A1 and A2). As in the published text, α itself can be assigned to either piece.

(5) From analogy to correspondence. The analogy becomes a real connection once an origin o and a unit length E are fixed on L. For positive integers m, n, lay off the n-th part of the unit m times from o, to the right or to the left. This yields two endpoints.

Continuation on the next page (not on this folio): these endpoints are taken to correspond to +m/n and −m/n, and 0 corresponds to o. The map φ: Q → L is well defined and injective, and it preserves order and betweenness. In coordinates (my formulation): φ(m/n) is the point at signed distance m·(E/n) from o.

Implicit step (mine): well-definedness requires that m/n = m'/n' gives the same point. This holds because m·(1/n) = m'·(1/n') as lengths, by commensurability with the common measure E/(nn'). The manuscript does not state this.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.

Omission compared with the published 1872 text and with §1: the density property of the line is not listed among the point properties ('if p is in L, there are infinitely many points to its left and right'; in the 1872 print, the existence of points between any two). The published §2 has it as property III. The draft lists only order, transitivity, betweenness and the cut by a point.
Well-definedness of the point m/n under change of representation (m/n = km/kn) is tacitly assumed (filled in by me).

results.what: Order axioms for points of a line (total order via right/left, transitivity, betweenness, segments, decomposition of the line by a point into two pieces with every point of one piece right of every point of the other)
results.modern_name: Linear order on a line / order (betweenness) axioms; decomposition of a linear order by an element
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind, Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen (1872), §2; axiomatized for geometry later by Pasch (1882) and Hilbert (1899)

results.what: Order-preserving embedding of Q into the line via origin and unit length (m/n laid off as m copies of E/n)
results.modern_name: Coordinatization of the line by rationals; order embedding Q -> line
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euclid/Descartes); formulated this way in Dedekind 1872 §2

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of §2 of the published 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872), close to the printed wording. It is elementary order material, well known as Dedekind's. The only interest is philological: the density property is absent here, and the variants 'Stück'/'Strecke' appear.

checkable.asserts: Example of the order that the embedding preserves: 3/4 lies right of 2/3
Well-definedness: m copies of E/n equal km copies of E/(kn) (3/4 = 6/8)

checkable.sympy: And(Rational(1,2) > Rational(1,3), Rational(1,3) > Rational(1,5), Rational(1,2) > Rational(1,5))

checkable.asserts: Laying off E/n m times to the left gives the point of -m/n
Next page's claim: the diagonal of the unit square is incommensurable, so its point corresponds to no rational

transcription_corrections: Heading: the struck word before 'Punkten' is a short cancelled word, probably 'den'; acceptable as transcribed.

'die Richtung der Strecke von β nach α' — the image shows corrections around 'β' and 'α' (struck letters before 'nach' and before 'α'); the reading 'von β nach α' is consistent with the sense and the 1872 print.

'Ist ferner[?]' at the end of the line: the image shows a word ending with a colon-like mark that seems superseded by the next line's 'liegt α rechts von β'. Probably 'Ist ferner' was left unfinished or replaced by the 'Liegt ferner ...' construction of the print. The word remains uncertain.
'Längeneinheit {+E+}[?]': the inserted mark under/after 'Län-' and before 'festgesetzt' is a small superscript letter, uncertain (possibly 'E' or 'ε'); reading uncertain.
'eine {+Stück+} Strecke': 'Stück' is written above 'Strecke' as an interlinear alternative; it is not clear which was meant to stand.
